title: Econ Slicer Engine for Multi-Tenant Route Profiling
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a backend service (Econ Slicer) that computes per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns for the Console and downstream billing/chargeback pipelines. The service must produce deterministic, explainable attributions for batched and streaming requests, account for KV-cache reuse and prefix caching, and surface confidence scores when fallbacks or multi-model routing occur. Outputs must be queryable by the Console (near-real-time) and consumable by the billing ingestion pipeline (hourly batch). The system should prioritize correctness and auditability, with configurable aggregation windows and deterministic tie-breaking rules so finance and customers can reconcile billed amounts against runtime traces.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route/per-model/per-customer breakdown exported as a flat time-series that joins to existing telemetry keys (route_id, model_variant, tenant_id)
Baseline accuracy: computed cost and latency within 2% of ground-truth synthetic replay for 99% of sampled traces
Freshness: Console queries show breakdowns with <=30s delay for recent windows and hourly rollups available for billing ingestion
Attribution correctness for batched requests: token-level apportioning across prompting, generation, and multipass reranking preserved
KV/prefix cache accounting: cache hits reduce attributed incremental compute; cache ownership deterministically assigned to request that primed the cache
Fallthrough handling: when routing falls back to a cheaper/compatible model, attribute to the executed variant and log policy reason with a confidence tag
Tests: unit, integration and load tests added; load test demonstrates stable compute under 5k reqs/s with 95th latency budget for slice compute
Runbook and reconciliation playbook delivered; Console visualizations wired to new endpoints
comments: 2026-02-11 — Kickoff: scoped core outputs (flat per-minute time series, attribution tags, confidence scores). Agreed to support both streaming query path and hourly rollups for billing. Action: prototype attribution algorithm on sampled traces (Ethan).

2026-02-18 — Design review: chose deterministic token-apportion algorithm (weighted by model token-cost & prompt proportion) vs heuristic average. PM requested add explicit handling for multi-model rollouts and canary traffic. Sofia to add tie-breaking rules to design doc.

2026-02-24 — Prototype: initial Go service that consumes runtime traces and emits per-request slices. Early findings: KV-cache ownership ambiguous when priming happens concurrently; decided to adopt 'first-writer' assignment with 10s grace window. Added unit tests for race scenarios.

2026-03-02 — Integration: wired prototype to analytics pipeline (stream processor) and produced first hourly rollups. Compared against replay-based ground truth: median error 1.4%, 99th percentile error 2.5% on synthetic workload (edge cases remain for very long sequences).

2026-03-04 — Review feedback from Finance: require export format to include human-readable rationale field for any attribution adjusted by >5%. Also add canonical mapping table for internal route tags to customer-facing product names. Added tickets: ENG-317003 (export rationale formatter).

2026-03-05 — Blocker discovered: high-cardinality tenant tag explosion when we materialize per-customer-per-model slices for short windows. Interim mitigation: enforce sampling + on-demand expansion for <7d queries. Follow-up: optimization task to add cold-storage compaction and retention policy (ENG-318210).
implementation_notes: Language: Go for low-latency streaming, small spark job for hourly rollups
Streaming path: consume enriched runtime traces (route_id, model_variant, token_counts, cache_events) via streaming topic, apply deterministic apportioner, emit slices to OLAP topic
Batch path: hourly aggregator produces aggregated rollups for billing; pre-aggregation keys are (tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, window_start)
Schema: flat slice record with fields: timestamp, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, attributed_tokens, compute_cost_usd, latency_ms_p50_p95, attribution_reason_code, confidence_score
Observability: per-window compute cost counters, error budget burn-rate, and reconciliation delta gauges compared to replay
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cardinality explosion for per-tenant short-window slices — Mitigation: sampling + on-demand expansion + TTL compaction
Risk: mismatch vs billing due to rounding/quantization — Mitigation: add high-precision reconciliation job and export rationale for adjustments
Risk: attribution disagreement with product owners on multi-model rollouts — Mitigation: expose confidence_score and store chosen policy version used for attribution
Risk: PII leakage through route metadata — Mitigation: scrub customer-identifying fields and require security review (see security_review_required)
next_steps: Run 24h production shadow of the slicer on a subset of tenants and compare to billing ledger
Add Console visualizations and wire to new slice endpoints
